title: MoE Ethiopian Exit Exam: Plant Science (2015)
description: Official Ministry of Education (MoE) Ethiopian University Exit Examination for Plant Science (2015). Complete with detailed explanations.

questions.questionText: If you want to test the germination percentage of wheat seeds under laboratory conditions, what type of experimental design you are going to choose?
questions.explanation: CRD (Completely Randomized Design) is often used for testing germination percentages.

questions.questionText: Farmer participatory research concept emerged as a response to?
options: Because small farmers did not adopt the technology packages developed at research stations
Generation of inappropriate technologies by scientists at research stations whose work was based on the transfer-of-technology model
questions.explanation: All options reflect reasons for the emergence of farmer participatory research.

questions.questionText: Which post-harvest operation is conducted to remove field heats in harvested fruits and vegetables?
questions.explanation: Pre-cooling is essential to remove field heat and prolong shelf life.

questions.questionText: Which one is correct about planning and establishing an orchard?
options: Fruit crops should be established in an area with suitable climatic and soil conditions which are favorable for the selected species and varieties
Standard planting type can be applied in area with steep slope usually greater than 25%
Hexagonal planting pattern is important in providing additional income at the early stage of the orchard
questions.explanation: Establishing fruit crops in suitable conditions is crucial for success.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not considered during fruit and vegetable nursery site selection?
options: Source of seeds to be planted
questions.explanation: Source of seeds is typically not a site selection factor.

questions.questionText: Conservation tillage has advantages over conventional tillage except?
options: Higher soil infiltration and moisture conservation
Reduces the opportunity for overwintering/oversummering of pests
No need to repeat the process
questions.explanation: Conservation tillage still requires periodic management.

questions.questionText: A combination of high Auxin and low cytokinin is used for culture of _____?
questions.explanation: High Auxin promotes root formation.

questions.questionText: Which statement is not correct about data collection and analysis?
options: Discuss how you will present and analyze your data
Describe exactly how you are going to collect your data
Describe how you are going to proceed in using questions or interview
questions.explanation: All statements are correct regarding data collection and analysis.

questions.questionText: The experimental design which allows blocking in two directions is called?
questions.explanation: CRBD (Complete Randomized Block Design) allows for two-way blocking.

questions.questionText: The herbicides that kill employed for general vegetation control on industrial sites, fallow land, and in aquatics are?
questions.explanation: Non-selective herbicides kill all vegetation.

questions.questionText: Which pathogen is responsible for causing 'late blight' of potato?
questions.explanation: Phytophthora infestans is the causative agent of late blight.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not the negative impact of weed?
questions.explanation: Weeds can actually be beneficial in scientific studies as they serve as model organisms for research on plant biology, herbicide resistance, and ecological studies. The other options are legitimate negative impacts of weeds.

questions.questionText: The association of a weed with a particular crop is due to?
questions.explanation: All factors can contribute to weed-crop associations.

questions.questionText: Which of the following statement is false regarding depth of seed and factors affecting seed depth?
options: Crops having bigger size sown at deeper depth while smaller seeds sown at shallower depth.
In relatively dry weather seeds sown deeply to contact with moist soil.
Seed placement in heavy (clay) soils should be shallow and deep in light (sandy) soils.
In fertile soil area seed sown at deeper depth than low soil fertility.
questions.explanation: Seeds are typically sown shallower in fertile soils.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the most widely used medium for tissue culture now?
questions.explanation: MS media is the most commonly used medium in tissue culture.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not correct about the relation between soil test result and fertilizer application?
options: When soil test result shows adequate nutrient level, the applied fertilizer may increase yields and the added yield will pay back the expense of the additional fertilizer.
When soil test result shows very low nutrient level, yield response to applied fertilizer is expected to be dramatic and profitable.
When soil test result shows high nutrient level, applied fertilizer will not increase yield.
When soil test result shows very high or excess nutrient levels, the yield may be reduced due to toxicity or imbalances of nutrients.
questions.explanation: When soil tests show adequate nutrient levels, additional fertilizer application is typically not economical as it will not significantly increase yields enough to justify the expense. This makes option A incorrect while the other statements accurately reflect the relationship between soil test results and fertilizer application.

questions.questionText: Which one is true about plant cell wall?
options: It is hydrophobic and is selectively permeable in nature.
Store DNA or hereditary information required for cell division, metabolism, and growth.
Maintain turgor pressure by maintaining a particular balance of ions, which causes the vacuole to swell against the cell wall.
Provides protection and prevents water loss from the cell.
questions.explanation: The cell wall helps maintain turgor pressure.

questions.questionText: Plant biotechnology involves?
options: Rapid clonal propagation of desired genotype
questions.explanation: All options are aspects of plant biotechnology.

questions.questionText: Which one is not correct about the importance of fruits and vegetables consumption?
options: Fruits and vegetables are consumed in small quantities just to satisfy the daily nutritional requirements.
Fruits and vegetables are considered as staple foods and consumed daily in large quantities.
Several malnutrition problems in developing countries are caused due to insufficient consumption of fruits and vegetables.
questions.explanation: Fruits and vegetables are important for nutrition and are not just consumed in small quantities.

questions.questionText: All, EXCEPT ONE, are the objectives of hybridization?
questions.explanation: Creation of uniformity is not an objective of hybridization.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a manifestation of heterosis?
questions.explanation: Heterosis (hybrid vigor) typically manifests as increased yield, earlier maturity, wider adaptability, and improved resistance to diseases and pests. Disease susceptibility would be a negative trait and not a manifestation of heterosis, which is characterized by superior performance.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not types of Farmer Participatory Research?
questions.explanation: Experimental research is not a type of Farmer Participatory Research.

questions.questionText: Which of the following crop is NOT originated in Abyssinian Center?
questions.explanation: Maize is not native to the Abyssinian Center.

questions.questionText: What should be the criteria for applying CRBD?
options: Fertility gradient in field is in two directions
Fertility gradient in field is in one direction only
questions.explanation: CRBD is applied when there is a fertility gradient in two directions.

questions.questionText: Which one is not a processing method used to extend the shelf-life of fruits for a long period of time?
questions.explanation: Packaging is not a processing method but a storage method.

questions.questionText: What is the role of soil in the production of food and development?
options: It serves as a medium for air and water circulation
It provides place and anchorage for plant growth and development
questions.explanation: Soil plays multiple roles in food production.

questions.questionText: From the following statement, one is true about water potential (Yw)?
options: Water potential (Yw) of pure water is one (by definition).
Adding of solutes & other forces increase water potential (Yw > 0)
For living organisms, water potential (Yw) is negative.
The negative hydrostatic pressure or tension pressure in the xylem cells raises water potential.
questions.explanation: Water potential in living organisms is typically negative.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is wrong about the Principles of Weed Management method?
options: Preventive is limitation of spread or dissemination and the establishment of weeds, to avoid new weed species
Eradication is a removal or control of certain weed species but not totally.
Control measure is limitation of already existing weed infestation or reduces the weed infestation
In weed management prevention and control are usually practiced, whereas eradication is exercised.
questions.explanation: Eradication refers to the complete removal of a weed species from an area, not partial control. Eradication aims to eliminate all viable vegetative and reproductive plant parts, while control only aims to limit the infestation. This makes option B incorrect.

questions.questionText: Regarding hormones and their function select the miss-matched choices?
options: Auxin = helps in promoting bud dormancy and senescence of leaves
Gibberellin = involved in the elongation of the stem, flowering and seed germination.
Cytokinins = involved in promoting cell division
Ethylene = Induce leaf senescence and fruit ripening
questions.explanation: Auxin does not promote dormancy; it promotes growth.

questions.questionText: Which one is true about managements applied to fruit and vegetable crops farm?
options: Irrigation is applied in areas where there is enough natural rainfall for growth and development of fruits and vegetables
The only means of controlling viral diseases in fruits and vegetables is using resistant varieties
Pruning is mainly applied to control shape and size while training is mainly applied to maintain productivity of the fruit crops
questions.explanation: Pruning and training serve different purposes in crop management.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT true about Pedigree breeding method?
options: Selection starts at F6 or F7
It takes less time than bulk method
questions.explanation: Natural selection can affect all breeding methods.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about the use of improved seed?
questions.explanation: Improved seeds typically enhance productivity.

questions.questionText: The effect of duration of light on the growth, reproduction (flowering) of a plant is known as?
questions.explanation: Photoperiodism refers to the response of plants to light duration.

questions.questionText: All are the characters of C3 plants except?
options: They have low net assimilation rate but high compensation point.
They have lower water use efficiency.
The initial product of C assimilation is the three 'C' compounds.
They are drought resistant & they are able to grow better even under moisture stress.
questions.explanation: C3 plants are generally not drought resistant.

questions.questionText: Which is the most commonly used design in field experiments?
questions.explanation: CRD is widely used due to its simplicity.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not among Herbicides formulated to facilitate their handling, storage, and application to improve their effectiveness under field conditions.
questions.explanation: Adjuvants are not herbicides but additives.

questions.questionText: Haploid plants are produced from?
questions.explanation: Haploids can be produced from both anthers and ovaries.

questions.questionText: From the following alternatives, select the wrong statement about plant growth and development.
options: Development is a qualitative change while growth is quantitative.
Growth is irreversible change in mass while development is irreversible change in state.
Development is a continuous process whereas growth is a phase-to-phase process.
As initiation of leaves and flower for development cell division is for growth.
questions.explanation: Cell division is part of both growth and development.

questions.questionText: Which one is true about propagation methods applied to fruit crops?
options: Sexual propagation involves genetic exchange of the materials so that there will be genetic segregation of the fruit crop.
Vegetative propagation does not involve genetic exchange of the materials so that production of clones can be achieved.
Grafting and budding are achieved by joining two separate parts of the fruit crop called 'Scion' and 'Root-stock'?
questions.explanation: All statements are true regarding propagation methods.

questions.questionText: Which one is true about cool-season vegetable crops?
options: They are normally adapted to low temperature.
They are normally adapted to high temperature.
They are sensitive to chilling temperature than warm-season vegetable crops.
questions.explanation: Cool-season crops thrive in lower temperatures.

questions.questionText: Which one is false about different phases of mono sigmoid growth curve?
options: Lag phase is characterized with maximum rate of dry matter accumulation.
In log phase rate of photosynthesis is higher than rate of respiration.
Log phase is a rapid development stage and known by an exponential phase.
Senescence phase is characterized by static growth rate and redistribution of dry matter into reproductive organs.
questions.explanation: Lag phase is not characterized by maximum accumulation.

questions.questionText: One of the following is the ability of the soil to provide all essential plant nutrients in available forms and in a suitable balance (suitable proportion)?
questions.explanation: Soil fertility refers to the soil's ability to provide nutrients.

questions.questionText: ________Seeds released from the mother plant in non-dormant state?
questions.explanation: The question is incorrectly phrased or the answer is wrong. Primary dormancy refers to seeds that ARE dormant when dispersed from the mother plant. Non-dormant seeds would not have primary dormancy. Secondary dormancy develops after dispersal due to unfavorable environmental conditions.

questions.questionText: Latin Square Design control --------------------- way variation?
questions.explanation: Latin Square Design controls variation in two directions.

questions.questionText: Which of the following problems are commonly observed in the fruit and vegetable production sectors of Ethiopia?
options: Lack of research and extension services
questions.explanation: All listed problems are common in Ethiopia's fruit and vegetable sector.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not among the factors that determine time and placement of fertilizers?
options: Solubility, mobility, toxicity, and rate of the fertilizer itself
questions.explanation: All listed factors determine fertilizer timing and placement.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is seed certification in Ethiopia?
questions.explanation: UPOV is the organization related to seed certification.

questions.questionText: Preservation of germplasm in frozen state termed as ______________?
questions.explanation: Cryopreservation is the method used for germplasm preservation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not advantages of Principles of Integrated Weed Management (IWM)?
options: Prevents resistance in weeds to herbicides
It shifts the crop-weed competition in favor of crop
questions.explanation: IWM actually reduces environmental pollution, not contributes to it. The statement 'It affects environmental pollution' is imprecise - IWM affects it positively by reducing it. All other options are genuine advantages of Integrated Weed Management.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not true about the characteristics of weed?
questions.explanation: Weeds do not differ significantly in seed characteristics.

questions.questionText: Which of the following tissue culture type could be used for virus cleaning?
questions.explanation: Meristem culture is effective for virus cleaning.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT true about Backcross Breeding Method?
options: The genotype of new variety is >96% identical with that of recurrent parent
Much smaller populations are needed as compared to pedigree method
The new variety cannot be superior to the recurrent parent in all characters
The character to be transferred by backcross method must have high heritability
questions.explanation: Backcross breeding can produce superior varieties.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT true about Pure-line selection?
options: Used both in self & cross pollinated crops
No need to repeat the process
questions.explanation: Pure-line selection often requires repeated testing.

questions.questionText: Due to climatological or socio-economic conditions growing of only one crop on a piece of land year after year is known as?
questions.explanation: Monocropping refers to growing a single crop repeatedly.

questions.questionText: Herbicide calibration for tractor mounted sprayers, if mark out 20m * 250m area with tall pegs that can easily be seen from a distance by a tractor driver. If the swath width is 4m the test plot can be covered in 5 passes and refill the tank and note the volume of H2O used in refilling the sprayer is 150 lts. Then how much of quantity of liquid sprayed /ha?
questions.explanation: The calculation shows that 208.3 lt/ha is the correct amount.

questions.questionText: One does not describe the feature of mixed cropping?
options: Its main objective is to utilize the space left between main crops
Its main objective is to get at least one crop under any hazard
All crops are given equal emphasis; there is no min or subsidiary crop
Sown without considering the population of either crop
questions.explanation: Mixed cropping often involves main and subsidiary crops.

questions.questionText: Management of plant disease by preventing its introduction into a previously uninvaded area is known as?
questions.explanation: Exclusion is the method to prevent disease introduction.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about the research purpose in Agriculture?
options: Solving problem related to crop/animal production and acquire new knowledge on this area
To create news to the media outlet
To defend government policy related to agriculture
questions.explanation: Research in agriculture aims to solve production problems.

questions.questionText: What are the three factors responsible for plant disease occurrence?
options: Susceptible host, avirulent pathogen and favorable environment
Resistant host, virulent pathogen and favorable environment
Susceptible host, virulent pathogen and favorable environment
questions.explanation: The presence of a susceptible host, virulent pathogen, and favorable environment leads to disease.

questions.questionText: What should be done to improve the production and productivity of fruit and vegetable crops at small scale peasant holdings of Ethiopia?
options: Improve availability and accessibility of production inputs
Develop and apply suitable crop management technologies
Improve transportation infrastructures and post-harvest handling facilities
questions.explanation: All measures are necessary for improvement.

questions.questionText: A particular microorganism you isolated from the diseased wheat plant may have caused the disease but you cannot find published or other information verifying this. Which procedure do you follow to verify whether this pathogen causes this disease?
questions.explanation: Koch's postulates are used to establish causation.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a vegetable growing structure?
questions.explanation: A nursery is not specifically a growing structure.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not a mechanism by which nutrients reach to root surface?
questions.explanation: Xylem transport is not a mechanism for nutrient uptake.

questions.questionText: Plant Pathology deals with the study of?
options: The microorganisms and the environmental factors that cause disease in plants
The mechanisms by the causal factors induce disease
The methods of preventing or managing disease
questions.explanation: Plant pathology encompasses all these aspects.

questions.questionText: If wheat plants begin to show disease symptoms because they were attacked by a foliar fungal pathogen, this is an example of?
questions.explanation: Fungal pathogens are biotic factors causing disease.

questions.questionText: Which environmental factor/s needs to be controlled to prolong the shelf-life of fruits and vegetables?
questions.explanation: All listed factors are crucial for extending shelf life.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is NOT a cross-pollinated crop?
questions.explanation: Potato is primarily self-pollinated.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a source of Bt/cry gene?
questions.explanation: Bacillus thuringiensis is the source of the Bt gene.

questions.questionText: Which of the following trait is NOT a quantitative trait?
questions.explanation: Seed color is a qualitative trait, not quantitative.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not among physical properties of the soil that affects soil fertility?
questions.explanation: Soil pH is a chemical property of soil, not a physical property. Physical properties include soil structure, texture, porosity, density, and water-holding capacity. Soil pH affects nutrient availability and microbial activity, determining soil fertility from a chemical perspective.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not the type of research based on the basic aim of the research?
questions.explanation: Survey research is a method, not a type based on aim.

questions.questionText: Which is/are issue/s related to the use of chemical pesticides?
options: Poisonous risks on humans and animals
questions.explanation: All listed issues are associated with chemical pesticide use.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a measure of vegetable seed physiological quality?
questions.explanation: All options are measures of seed quality.

questions.questionText: As compared with aerobic respiration, anaerobic respiration (fermentation) of one molecule of glucose is?
options: Utilizes all the three stages of respiration (glycolysis, Krebs cycle, ETC)
Produces less energy yield (releases 1/20th energy as compared to aerobic)
Takes place both in mitochondria and cytoplasm
questions.explanation: Anaerobic respiration yields significantly less energy.

questions.questionText: All are correct about the sequence of crops (principles of crop rotation) except?
options: The target crop should be planted immediately after the legumes or fallow period
Crops, which are deep feeders, should alternate with shallow feeders.
Crops that are botanically similar should not normally follow each other in the rotation.
questions.explanation: All statements are correct regarding crop rotation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is not advantages of Principles of Integrated Weed Management (IWM)?
options: Prevents resistance in weeds to herbicides
It shifts the crop-weed competition in favor of crop
questions.explanation: IWM aims to reduce environmental pollution.

questions.questionText: Which of the following groups of essential elements for plant growth are classified as macronutrients?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Sulphur, and Potassium are macronutrients.

questions.questionText: The direction of the block in CRBD is --------------------------- to the gradient?
questions.explanation: In Completely Randomized Block Design (CRBD), blocks are arranged perpendicular to the gradient of fertility or other variation to capture maximum variability within each block. This allows the treatments to be compared within relatively homogeneous blocks, reducing experimental error.

questions.questionText: Degree of freedom in CRBD compared with CRD using the same material is?
questions.explanation: The degree of freedom for error in CRBD is less than in CRD when using the same materials. This is because CRBD accounts for block effects, which reduces the error degrees of freedom by (r-1) where r is the number of blocks or replications.

questions.questionText: One of the following is not among Herbicides formulated to facilitate their handling, storage, and application to improve their effectiveness under field conditions.
questions.explanation: Adjuvants are not herbicides but additives.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is wrong about the Principles of Weed Management method?
options: Preventive is limitation of spread or dissemination and the establishment of weeds, to avoid new weed species
Eradication is a removal or control of certain weed species but not totally.
Control measure is limitation of already existing weed infestation or reduces the weed infestation
In weed management prevention and control are usually practiced, whereas eradication is exercised.
questions.explanation: Eradication aims for total removal, not partial control.

questions.questionText: What will be the direction of the flow of water when a plant cell is placed in a hypotonic solution?
options: Water will flow into the cell
No flow of water in any direction
Water will flow in both directions
Water will flow out of the cell
questions.explanation: In a hypotonic solution, water flows into the cell.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following groups of fruits correctly classified based on their respiratory pattern?
questions.explanation: The first group includes climacteric fruits that continue to ripen after harvest.

questions.questionText: What is the reason behind high perishability of fruits and vegetables after harvest?
options: Because they are harvested at immature stage
Because they remain dormant after harvest and do not involve in metabolic reaction and enzymatic process
Because they are living after harvest and continue their ontogeny process
questions.explanation: Fruits and vegetables are living tissues that continue metabolic processes.

questions.questionText: Quick growing crops used as substitutes for staple crops that have failed on account of unfavorable conditions is called?
questions.explanation: Catch crops are planted to quickly utilize available resources.

questions.questionText: Variety that must be different from the existing variety at least by one trait is called ------------?
questions.explanation: Distinctness refers to the requirement for variety differentiation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following breeding method is different?
questions.explanation: Heterosis breeding focuses on hybrid vigor, unlike the others.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is not a cultural method of plant disease management?
questions.explanation: All listed methods are cultural practices for disease management.

questions.questionText: What is the aim of integrated soil fertility management?
options: Optimizing agronomic use efficiency of the applied nutrients
To utilize all the possible sources of inputs in a careful and efficient manner
questions.explanation: All options reflect the aims of integrated soil fertility management.

questions.questionText: Which is correctly ordered about the style of citation (reference)?
options: Year of publication, Author(s), Title of work, publication date
Author, year of publication, Title of work, publication date, city of publication
Title of work, Author, Year of publication, publication date, city of publication
Publication data, Authors, Title of work, year of publication, city of publication
questions.explanation: The correct citation order typically follows: Author(s), year of publication, title of work, publication details (which may include journal name, volume, pages, or for books, the publisher and city of publication). This follows standard academic citation formats like APA, MLA, and Chicago style.

questions.questionText: Plant Hormone is a naturally-occurring compound which regulates change in physiology, growth or development of the plant. Among the following which one is responsible to control dwarfness of the plant?
questions.explanation: Gibberellins (GA) are responsible for controlling dwarfness in plants.

questions.questionText: Plant cell type which are alive at maturity and have only a primary wall; provide mechanical support during growth?
questions.explanation: Collenchyma cells are living at maturity, have primary walls with uneven thickenings rich in pectin and hemicellulose, and provide mechanical support to growing plant parts. Sclerenchyma cells are typically dead at maturity with thick secondary walls, while parenchyma cells are thin-walled and serve for storage and metabolism rather than primary mechanical support.

questions.questionText: A solution is a homogeneous mixture of two or more components in which the particle size is smaller than 1 nm. In which type of solutions the cell shrinks when it is placed in this solution?
questions.explanation: In hypertonic solutions, water moves out of the cell causing it to shrink.

questions.questionText: The minerals absorbed by the roots are mineral ions dissolved in the soil and water. They support plants to complete their life cycle and are to produce seeds. Which of the following is present in the green pigment of the leaf?
questions.explanation: Magnesium (Mg) is a central component of chlorophyll, the green pigment in leaves.

questions.questionText: The rate at which water moves through the plants due to transpiration plays an important role in maintaining plant water balance. Which of the following is the instrument for measuring the rate of transpiration in plants?
questions.explanation: A potometer is used to measure the rate of water uptake (transpiration) in plants.

questions.questionText: Food preservation can be defined as the process of treating and handling food in such a way as to stop or greatly slow down spoilage and prevent foodborne illness while maintaining nutritional value, texture and flavor. Why is low temperature maintained for preservation?
questions.explanation: Low temperatures slow down bacterial growth, minimizing spoilage.

questions.questionText: What is an example of positive geotropism in plants?
questions.explanation: Positive geotropism (or gravitropism) is growth toward gravity, demonstrated by roots growing downward. Stems growing upward exhibit negative geotropism, lateral root growth is diagravitropism, and flower closing is a thigmotropic or nyctinastic response, not primarily gravitropic.

questions.questionText: As you will be a plant Agronomist in commercial crop farms and the area is characterized by erratic rainfall you need to plan to get high production within drought situation, what is your plan to achieve the above goal?
options: Maintaining water balance by irrigation supplements
questions.explanation: All options are valid strategies for managing drought conditions.

questions.questionText: Simultaneous fusion of the generative nuclei one with egg cell and other with the endospermic nuclei is termed?
questions.explanation: Double fertilization is unique to angiosperms where one sperm fertilizes the egg and another fertilizes the endosperm.

questions.questionText: The Rudimentary root of the seed or seedling that forms the primary root of the young plant is called as?
questions.explanation: The radicle is the embryonic root that develops into the primary root.
